newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela and Trinidad plan petroleum alliance.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela and Trinidad plan petroleum alliance.

text.p: Venezuela and Trinidad and Tobago are considering a strategic alliance in Trinidad's 165,000 barrel per day (bpd) Pointe a Pierre refinery that could mean Venezuela supplying 60,000 bpd of crude oil to the plant, Venezuela's foreign ministry said in a statement on Monday.

The plan was part of a wide-ranging energy cooperation between the neighbours, including forming joint companies to develop natural gas fields near their marine border, particularly the Tajali, Loran and Cocuina fields.
The crude supply idea would involve increasing the capacity of Pointe a Pierre to cater for Venezuela's heavy crudes.
Other plans include Venezuela exporting electricity to Trinidad and the formation of a retailing joint-venture between Trinidad's National Petroleum Marketing Company and Venezuela's Maraven.

Trinidad and Tobago's Prime Minister Basdeo Panday is due to arrive in Venezuela on Tuesday to meet Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera. Relations betweeen the two countries have been upset recently by disagreements over fishing and petroleum exploration rights around their marine border.
